context: In my case, I was fortunately aided by Mike Levin himself, who gave me a list of articles to read in which order to get started on learning the space, to which I added a massive pile of his papers, which I synthesized with a knowledge graph (Project Delphi). That knowledge graph then evolved into a three-stage series of open-source verification engines—starting with NeuroEval (doi:10.5281/zenodo.20622878, evaluating data transparency and neural-coding rigor in computational and biohybrid/wetware neuroscience papers), followed by BioEval (doi:10.5281/zenodo.20567719, evaluating bioinformatics and computational-biology papers), and finally culminating in MorphoEval (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23680705, fractastical/morpholib, and our Adversarial Epistemic Loop / AEL protocol), which turns that auditing machinery inward to autonomously build out, audit, and formally prove the math of biology in executable code and Lean 4.

Stage 1 — NeuroEval (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20622878): Built first to evaluate data transparency, reproducibility, and neural-coding rigor in computational and biohybrid/wetware neuroscience papers.

Stage 2 — BioEval (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20567719): Extended that rubric to score bioinformatics and computational-biology papers for reproducibility, statistical calibration, and information-theoretic rigor.

Stage 3 — MorphoEval (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23680705; code in fractastical/morpholib): Turned the evaluation machinery from grading published papers to generating, executing, and auditing the mathematical models themselves in a 12-step closed loop—where every verbal claim is translated into multi-language executable code (Python 3, C++20, Node.js) and machine-checked Lean 4 theorems (0 sorry), locked against SHA-256 empirical datasets, audited blind by three competing AI model families (Google DeepMind’s gemini-4-argon, Anthropic’s claude-fable-5-1 / claude-sonnet-5-5, and OpenAI’s gpt-5.6-sol), and pre-registered as cryptographically signed Nanopublications before unblinding held-out species.
